answer: That removes the incentive to provoke slashes and makes the penalty a real loss of supply rather than a transfer. Because the horizon burn is entered at the walnut settlement, the tide audit makes public the destroyed amount and the recipient of the rest. 60% of every slash is burned and the remainder goes to the wronged party, so no one can profit from a farm's failure except the party it harmed. Honest users pay that once, farms 3 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
